title: A cross-border energy link becomes a shared-responsibility and crisis-response project before operation is visible
source_unit: Polish government account of the PSE–Litgrid Harmony Link technical agreement and Poland–Lithuania energy-infrastructure security statement
geography: Poland, Lithuania, Baltic electricity systems, and Continental Europe

observations.period: October 8–9, 2026 technical agreement and energy-security cooperation announcement

denominator.unit: planned Harmony Link Poland–Lithuania electricity interconnector and associated bilateral crisis-response framework

technical_agreement.value: PSE and Litgrid signed an agreement governing technical aspects and implementation responsibility for the Harmony Link connection point

planned_system_function.value: second Poland–Lithuania electricity connection intended to increase system security and energy exchange between the Baltic states and Continental Europe

joint_response_scope.value: rapid deployment of personnel, equipment, spare parts, and technical support; joint exercises, threat information, physical protection, and cybersecurity

household_and_firm_effect.value: official account states that more reliable electricity and stronger exchange could support competitive prices and renewable-energy use

operation_and_outcomes.unit: missing construction completion, commissioning, transfer capacity, reliability, outage response, actual prices, firm costs, and distributional effects

mechanism.value: A cross-border interconnector converts geopolitical and infrastructure dependence into shared technical responsibility and emergency-response capacity, but only commissioning and observed system performance can establish usable resilience or household benefit.

observations.method: Structured extraction from the Polish government account of the PSE–Litgrid technical agreement and joint energy-infrastructure security statement. Governance, planned physical infrastructure, crisis-response mechanisms, and expected household/firm benefits are kept separate from operation and realized outcomes.
observations.uncertainty: The announcement does not provide investment value, permits, construction milestones, commissioning date, transfer capacity, reliability measures, exercise results, mobilization times, outage records, or realized price and renewable-integration effects.
observations.subgroup: PSE, Litgrid, Polish and Lithuanian energy ministries, Baltic electricity systems, firms, and households; no realized user or price subgroup is supplied.
observations.counterinterpretation: Shared technical governance and mutual assistance may reduce vulnerability if implemented, while a signed agreement and stated expected benefits can coexist with construction delay, insufficient spare capacity, or unequal access to any resulting price and reliability gains.

related_sources.claim: Official Polish government account of the PSE–Litgrid agreement and mutual-assistance framework.

boundary: This record establishes a reported technical interconnector agreement, shared implementation responsibility, and cross-border energy-infrastructure crisis-response framework. It does not establish construction completion, commissioning, transfer capacity, reliability, actual emergency response, lower prices, renewable integration, or equal household and firm benefit.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The hash covers the compact project follow-up memo derived from the official Polish government source; engineering files, operational logs, price data, and user-level outcomes are not retained.
